entries.name: Silk Test
entries.definition: A tool for automating functional and regression tests of software applications, now sold by Micro Focus.

entries.name: Simple interrupted suture
entries.definition: A basic suturing technique in which each stitch is placed and knotted separately to close a wound.

entries.name: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
entries.definition: The internet protocol used to send email from mail clients to servers and between mail servers.

entries.name: Simple Public Key Infrastructure
entries.definition: An IETF proposal for authorisation certificates that bind permissions to public keys instead of names, described in RFC 2693.

entries.name: SimpleLegal
entries.definition: Software for corporate legal departments to manage matters, outside counsel invoices and legal spend.

entries.name: Simputer
entries.definition: A low-cost handheld computer designed in India in the early 2000s for people with little access to computers, using icons and speech output.

entries.name: Single In-Line Memory Module
entries.definition: An older type of computer memory module with contacts on both sides of one edge that are electrically the same.

entries.name: Single sign-on
entries.definition: An authentication approach that lets a user sign in once to reach several separate applications.

entries.name: Site reliability engineering
entries.definition: Applying software engineering to running large systems so that they stay reliable, scalable and efficient.

entries.name: Skip tracing
entries.definition: Locating a person who has moved or disappeared, such as a debtor, by searching records and databases.

entries.name: Sluice gate
entries.definition: A movable barrier that controls the flow of water in a channel, dam or canal.

entries.name: Slurm Workload Manager
entries.definition: An open-source job scheduler and resource manager for Linux computing clusters.

entries.name: Smart buildings
entries.definition: Buildings that use networked sensors, controls and software to automate and tune systems such as heating, lighting, security and energy use.

entries.name: Smart lighting
entries.definition: Lighting that can be controlled automatically or remotely, for example by sensors, schedules or an app.

entries.name: Smart meter systems
entries.definition: Electronic utility meters and the communications and software that send a customer's usage readings to the supplier.

entries.name: Smart pig
entries.definition: An instrumented device sent through a pipeline to inspect it for corrosion, cracks and dents.

entries.name: SmartBidNet
entries.definition: Online software for construction companies to invite subcontractors to bid and to manage bid documents and responses.

entries.name: Smartphone operation
entries.definition: Using a smartphone's apps, settings and features for tasks such as calls, messaging and navigation.

entries.name: Snort
entries.definition: An open-source network intrusion detection and prevention system that inspects traffic against rules.

entries.name: Snow Software
entries.definition: A software asset management platform, from the company Snow Software, for tracking software licences and usage.

entries.name: Social and behavior change communication
entries.definition: A public-health communication approach that uses strategic messaging and community engagement to change both individual behaviours and the social norms around them.

entries.name: Social determinants of health
entries.definition: The non-medical conditions in which people live and work, such as income, housing and education, that shape their health.

entries.name: Social-emotional learning
entries.definition: An educational approach that teaches skills such as self-awareness, self-management, empathy, relationship skills and responsible decision-making.

entries.name: Social impact bond
entries.definition: A pay-for-success contract in which private investors fund a social programme and are repaid by government only if agreed outcomes are met.

entries.name: Social media advertising
entries.definition: Planning, buying and running paid advertisements on social media platforms.

entries.name: Social media analytics
entries.definition: Collecting and analysing data from social media accounts and conversations to measure performance and audience behaviour.

entries.name: Social media content creation
entries.definition: Planning and making posts, images, video and captions for an organisation's or person's social media accounts.

entries.name: Social media content management
entries.definition: Planning, scheduling, publishing and reviewing the content on social media accounts.

entries.name: Social media management
entries.definition: Running social media accounts for a person or organisation, including planning and publishing posts, replying to followers and reporting on results.

entries.name: Social media optimization
entries.definition: Using social media activity and content to raise the visibility of a brand or website and bring traffic to it.

entries.name: Social sustainability
entries.definition: The part of sustainability concerned with the wellbeing, equity and rights of the people and communities affected by an organisation or project.

entries.name: Sociology of education
entries.definition: The study of how schooling and education relate to social structures, inequality and social change.

entries.name: Socket 478
entries.definition: A 478-pin CPU socket made by Intel for later Pentium 4 and Celeron processors.

entries.name: Socket 5
entries.definition: A 320-pin CPU socket used by Intel for its Pentium processors from 75 to 133 MHz.

entries.name: SockJS
entries.definition: A JavaScript library that gives browsers a WebSocket-like object and falls back to other transports when WebSockets are unavailable.

entries.name: Softrax
entries.definition: Software for revenue recognition, billing and contract management, aimed at software and subscription companies.

entries.name: Software architecture
entries.definition: Designing software structure and major component interactions.

entries.name: Software as a service
entries.definition: A way of delivering software over the internet by subscription, hosted by the provider instead of installed by the customer.

entries.name: Software-defined WAN
entries.definition: A way of running a wide area network in which software centrally controls how traffic is routed across links such as broadband, MPLS and cellular.

entries.name: Software engineering
entries.definition: Systematic design, construction and maintenance of software.
